newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU wants international action on Serb crisis.
newsitem.headline: EU wants international action on Serb crisis.

text.p: The European Union on Friday called on the international community to act over the Serb political crisis which it said was hindering the peace process in Bosnia-Herzegovina.
"The European Union continues to be deeply worried by the crisis in Republika Srpska," the Luxembourg EU presidency said in a statement.
"It is characterised by schemes which are in blatant contradiction with the progress of a normal democratic life, and by unacceptable intimidation and harrassment," it added.
"The international community therefore is duty bound to react in the face of this situation."

The EU reiterated its view that Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic acted constitutionally when she dissolved the Bosnian Serb parliament last week and it called on the political parties to work towards a peaceful solution to the feud.
Plavsic has been battling for control with hardliners loyal to Radovan Karadzic, the former Bosnian Serb president who still wields heavy behind-the-scenes power.

The EU called again on the various parties to respect the Dayton peace accords on Bosnia, which included an obligation to hand over indicted war criminals to the United Nations War Crimes Tribunal in the Hague.
On Thursday the European Commission had said it was cutting off reconstruction aid to the Bosnian Serbs until Karadzic, an indicted war criminal, was arrested.

The Republika Srpska, the Serb portion of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was due to receive 30 million European currency units ($34 million) from the Commission this year in aid to repair roads, telecommunications links and other reconstruction projects.

Separately on Thursday NATO-led peacekeepers in Bosnian Serb-controlled territory arrested Milan Kovacevic, director of Prijedor hospital, and shot dead a second suspect. Both men were sought by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in conection with ethnic cleansing operations in northern Bosnia in 1992,
The EU said it considered the peacekeepers' action had been "perfectly legitimate".
